items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Charlie said, 'I coughed go down to the Chicago Theater and hit Hank in his mouth... waited for Elvin, Ray and Hank to come off the stage.'

ctx.x: had enough to get out if we paid the fine. I said, 'Well, what is -- what would bail be, Your Honor?' Then it went up to three bills and something. Well, we didn't have enough, you know, to get out on bail, so we were forced to pay the fine. But I wasn't in too much of a hurry to pay the fine. I guess that was the right thing to do, but I was just stubborn, you know. And I had plans to fight the case through the NAACP, you know. Fair practice, you know. But they didn't see this, their way. So the Judge fined us.…

go down to the Chicago Theater, and waited for Elvin, Ray and Hank to come off the stage. And we got word to the doorman to tell Hank to come out in the alley. He came out, and we walked out on State Street, and we conversed. Charlie said, "Man, why would you leave me like that, without saying a word?" He said, "I've got a good mind to hit you in the mouth." You know, Charlie wasn't a fighter. He says -- Hank says, "Bells." And this really infuriated Charlie. Charlie said, "Come on, man, let's go, before I end up…
Did you actually look for a piano player?
